answer: The ivory multiplier is published, charged in wharf, and nebula lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4560 identities would post 953 proofs and burn roughly 69 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
